title: Gotrade Daily: Marvell Tonight, AI-Chip Trade Tested
summary: Marvell reports tonight, testing whether the AI-chip rally can broaden beyond Nvidia. Here is the watchlist and key catalysts before the US session.
body_markdown:
## Tonight's Watchlist


Stock Movement What to Watch


[MRVL](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/mrvl/) Down ~4% into the print Reports after close; focus on custom AI silicon and forward guidance


[NVDA](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/nvda/) Higher after last night's print Q3 guide above expectations; sets the tone for chip sentiment tonight


[AVGO](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/avgo/) Filled near publish Marvell's closest custom-silicon rival; reads through from MRVL


[AMD](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/amd/) Filled near publish A gauge of AI GPU demand beyond Nvidia


[AFRM](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/afrm/) Reports tonight A fintech and consumer read, outside the chip theme


## Tonight's Catalysts


### Marvell is the next AI-chip test


**Marvell ([MRVL](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/mrvl/) )** reports after the close. Analyst consensus points to revenue near US$2.71 billion and earnings per share around US$0.92. Marvell builds custom AI silicon, chips designed specifically for cloud giants, so its results are the cleanest read on whether AI spending is broadening beyond Nvidia. The stock fell about 4% into the print, a sign expectations are running high.


### Nvidia has already set the tone


**Nvidia ([NVDA](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/nvda/) )** posted data-center revenue of US$89 billion last night, up 117% year over year, and guided next quarter to US$108 billion. That upbeat tone lifted the whole chip complex. **Broadcom ([AVGO](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/avgo/) )** and **AMD ([AMD](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/amd/) )** often move in the same direction.


### Fintech and consumer also report


**Affirm ([AFRM](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/afrm/) )** also reports tonight, offering a read on consumer credit health and buy-now-pay-later adoption. Alongside several retailers reporting this week, it is a reminder that tonight is not only about chips.
